rationale_code: `startCodegenSession.handler` normalizes `options.outputPath`, creates that directory with `fs.mkdir`, starts an in-memory session, and returns `sessionId` plus options. It writes local filesystem/session state but does not return host file contents or contact an attacker host. [dropped destination_

`endCodegenSession.handler` selects a recorded session by `sessionId`, generates test code, writes it with `fs.writeFile` to a path derived from the session options, and returns paths/test code. This is a local write, not an attacker-readable destination by itself.
The handler returns the in-memory codegen session selected by `sessionId`; no network or host file read is shown. Exact session shape is in `ActionRecorder`, which was not included.
The handler deletes/clears an in-memory codegen session selected by `sessionId` and returns success; no external destination is shown.

The advertised `url` is an agent-chosen URL, and the handler creates a Playwright browser/page then dispatches to `navigationTool.execute`. A browser navigation sends a request to that chosen host. The concrete `NavigationTool` implementation is not included.

The tool is advertised to screenshot the current page/element. Current page pixels may be attacker-authored web content or non-public `file://`, localhost, or intranet content reached by the browser. The screenshot implementation is imported but not included, so exact return fields are undetermined.

Clicking an element in the current browser page can trigger navigation, form submission, or other requests to the page's host, including an attacker-chosen page. The concrete `ClickTool` implementation is not included.
Clicking inside an iframe can trigger requests or state changes in the framed page, which can be attacker-controlled. The concrete implementation is not included.
The advertised tool fills `value` into an iframe element; that agent-supplied value can be submitted or observed by an attacker-controlled page/frame. The concrete implementation is not included.
The advertised tool fills agent-supplied `value` into a page element; an attacker-controlled page can read or submit it. The concrete implementation is not included.
The advertised tool selects agent-supplied `value` in the current page, which can be observed/submitted by the current site. The concrete implementation is not included.
Hovering can trigger page JavaScript and network requests on an attacker-controlled current page. The concrete implementation is not included.

The advertised tool uploads a local `filePath` to a file input in the current page; if the page is attacker-controlled, this can deliver that file to an attacker-readable destination. The concrete implementation is not included.

The tool executes agent-supplied browser JavaScript. Such script can read page data and return it, including non-public localhost/intranet/file page data, and can send data to arbitrary network destinations from the page. If run on attacker-authored pages, returned data can be attacker-controlled. T

Console messages are registered from page `console` and `pageerror` events, and the tool is advertised to retrieve them. Page scripts and errors can be attacker-authored; logs may also contain non-public data from localhost/intranet/file pages. Exact execute output shape is not included.
The advertised tool changes browser viewport/device emulation settings. No return of page data or network send is shown. The concrete `ResizeTool` implementation is not included.
The handler closes the local browser instance and returns a fixed status string. It does not expose secrets or contact an attacker destination.

The tool performs HTTP GET to agent-chosen `url`; the handler creates a Playwright request context with `baseURL: url`. Responses from attacker hosts are untrusted, and responses from localhost/intranet URLs can be non-public. The concrete request implementation is not included.

The tool POSTs agent-supplied `value`/headers/token to agent-chosen `url`; returned responses can be attacker-controlled or non-public localhost/intranet data. The concrete request implementation is not included.

The tool PUTs agent-supplied `value`/headers/token to agent-chosen `url`; returned responses can be attacker-controlled or non-public localhost/intranet data. The concrete request implementation is not included.

The tool PATCHes agent-supplied `value`/headers/token to agent-chosen `url`; returned responses can be attacker-controlled or non-public localhost/intranet data. The concrete request implementation is not included.

The tool sends DELETE to agent-chosen `url`, possibly with token/headers; returned responses can be attacker-controlled or non-public localhost/intranet data. The concrete request implementation is not included.
The advertised tool registers a pending wait for a response matching `url` under `id` but does not itself contact a new URL or return the response body. The concrete implementation is not included.

The advertised tool waits for and validates a previously captured HTTP response body. That response may be from attacker-authored web content or from non-public localhost/intranet pages. The handler passes `userAgent` into browser settings and a new context can be created with that user agent. This stores browser configuration; no immediate external request or page-content return is shown. The concrete tool implementation is not included.

The advertised tool returns visible text from the current page. Current page text can be attacker-authored, or can be non-public content from file, localhost, or intranet pages reached by the browser. The concrete implementation is not included.

The advertised tool returns HTML from the current page. Page HTML can be attacker-authored, or non-public content from file, localhost, or intranet pages reached by the browser. The concrete implementation is not included.
Browser history navigation can issue requests to previously visited hosts, including attacker-chosen hosts from earlier navigation. The concrete implementation is not included.
Browser history navigation can issue requests to previously visited hosts, including attacker-chosen hosts from earlier navigation. The concrete implementation is not included.
Dragging elements in the current page can trigger page JavaScript and network/state changes on an attacker-controlled site. The concrete implementation is not included.
Key presses in the current page can enter/submit data or trigger requests to the current site, which may be attacker-controlled. The concrete implementation is not included.

The advertised tool saves the current page as a local PDF at `outputPath`/`filename`. A local filesystem write is not an attacker-readable sink under the stated threat model, and no return of page content is shown. The concrete implementation is not included.
Clicking a link can navigate/open a new tab and send requests to the linked host, including an attacker-controlled host. The concrete implementation is not included.
